text: Training our next generation of doctors and nurses in the art of navigating complex human conversations with humility and kindness should not be treated as less important than technical training.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: But sometimes, innovation can also be found in simply going back to mastery of the basics.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: In the case of healthcare, it is the art of treating people beyond the science of treating disease.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Renowned surgeon, Dr Atul Gawande, contends in his ground-breaking book "Being Mortal" that courageous doctors who help patients explore these three questions achieve far better outcomes for end-of-life care.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: One, what is more important to you than living longer?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: And three, what are you willing to give up to get the life you want in the time you have left?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: May we give them the ability to write something that is worth remembering?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Much has already been said by other Members of this House before about legislating caregiver leave and giving financial support, so I will not dwell on that but focus on issues of emotional and psychological support.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Navigating a fragmented landscape of caregivers' subsidies and services can be frustrating and intimidating to an average Singaporean, let alone one who is already acutely stressed by caregiving or limited in their English language proficiency.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, AIC plays intermediary between caregiving bodies and care receivers.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Could AIC consider having a team of AIC coordinators who can journey with our caregivers, especially those from the lower-income bracket, from start to end?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Caregivers need practical help to figure out where to start and how to end.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Just trying to make sense of the system might compound the emotional stress they are already under.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Frustrated caregivers might not have time or space to explore their options objectively.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: When they randomly cobble together their own solutions, they end up providing haphazard and even inappropriate care for their own loved ones.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: So, they do need someone experienced in the system to come alongside, help them coordinate their piecemeal needs to ensure the full range of needs of both caregiver and care receiver are adequately met.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Also, though there is a good range of formal care services already being offered in the landscape, from home therapy to adult day care, a Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) survey of 20,000 caregivers shows that usage of these services is surprisingly still very low.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: The coordinators' intervention can not only help to increase the take-up rates, it can also investigate the real reasons why utilisation remains low in the first place.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: That same MSF survey discovered that spousal caregivers and caregivers of lower socio-economic status are more likely to be badly impacted by caregiving.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Under siege, these caregivers may slip into depression or even some form of extreme behaviour like abuse of patient or abuse of self.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: An AIC coordinator can spot early signs of caregiver mental or physical breakdown and provide timely intervention.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: If we believe family should be the first line of support, we must keep finding ways to better support the very people trying their utmost to live out that value, especially those who are far less financially privileged than us.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: On the jobs of the future and being future-ready, as our economy transforms itself against the cyclical headwinds and structural changes, jobs need to be redesigned and keep pace with technology.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The questions I have are: what are the jobs that will be at risk in the healthcare sector as a result of automation, robotisation and job redesign?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: How can we better manage the foreseeable challenges to protect the interest of workers who will be affected?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What kind of programmes will be rolled out to assist affected workers to transit to other roles within and outside the industry?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What measures are taken and which policies are refined to attract more Singaporeans to work in the Intermediate Long-term Care (ILTC) sector?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In order to raise the overall standards of the healthcare industry, there is a need to refresh and refine the industry as a whole.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As our healthcare model evolves, the ILTC services will play a larger role.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, there is a need to make sure that this sector's services step up, transform and grow so that the standards of healthcare can also improve dramatically over a short period of time.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: From my involvement in the Healthcare Cluster Tripartite Workgroup, I have seen how collaboration on productivity improvement projects has brought benefits to the hospitals, employees and patients.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that closer collaboration amongst the ILTC organisations, MOH and healthcare union will help raise the level of ILTC industry practices and bring benefits to patients, too.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Such an association will help foster an ecosystem for the ILTC community to thrive in and enhance the professionalism of healthcare workers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It will serve to provide a platform for industry players to network, share concerns and challenges, and allow them to collaborate with one another.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As a start, MOH, through AIC, could provide manpower and resource support to speed up its formation.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As the demand for the healthcare sector rises, more needs to be done to encourage the public healthcare sector to make FWAs more pervasive across all institutions and all job types.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, there is a need to comply with the legislation and tripartite guidelines.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: We could share more stories and examples of staff who have successfully converted to FWAs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Increasingly, healthcare workers are facing more challenges to switch to FWAs due to higher expectations and demands at work.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: FWAs should be one that supports a pro-family environment and staff who decide to request for FWAs should also be accorded an equal level of recognition and opportunity for the work they produce.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Whilst the need of the organisation needs to be fulfilled, many are struggling to cope with caring for their families.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: We need to help them so that they can continue to work and contribute meaningfully to care for our patients.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is particularly critical for those who need advanced care and are treated with non-standard drugs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: During this volatile economic period, many of the mature workers are concerned about the uncertainty of their continuous employment and therefore the fear of losing their employers' medical benefit.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Alternatively, MOH could regularly review the list of non-standard drugs to standard drugs to bring down the costs of medication.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Long-term healthcare models in Nordic countries focus on home-care, rather than on hospital-based care for the sick elderly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Even with our residency programmes, aligning with the US' Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) guidelines, we do always have to grapple with explaining our heavy patient load to our site visitor every accreditation year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Our doctor-to-patient ratio quoted seems to fall within the global range given, as in a previous response to our Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: But when it comes to work on the shop floor, we are really, really, very busy and very heavily loaded.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: And in healthcare, Madam, the words automation, value chain, productivity and quality will have to take a customised definition.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share details about how it will provide our nurses with more career advancement opportunities, greater authority and autonomy, and implement flexible and part-time work arrangements?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What can be done to improve their work conditions and remuneration?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: However, the labour market is already tight across all industries and sectors.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: There is stiff competition for workers and control over foreign manpower will only get tighter.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Moreover, even as we look to leverage technology more, the human touch cannot be replaced in delivering quality care.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Therefore, I would like to ask, firstly, what is the Ministry's plan in tackling the manpower challenges in the ILTC sector.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How does the Ministry intend to attract more?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Thirdly, will the Ministry consider requiring and assisting ILTC providers to redesign their processes and systems where necessary, so that more older or retired workers can join to supplement the manpower needs?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I have the privilege of giving a response to Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Tin Pei Ling for their earlier cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Indeed, health promotion is a key plank of our active ageing initiatives under the Ministerial Committee on Ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is because good health is the basic condition for successful ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will expand our efforts to promote seniors' health both in the workplace and in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Many of our seniors are still gainfully employed and this is a good thing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is a good thing also in relation to mental health maintenance, as pointed out by many Members earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: HPB started with a programme at the taxi service centres for taxi drivers of the ComfortDelGro group in June 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: HPB knows that taxi drivers are always on the road and, therefore, have very little time to attend health-related activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By observing their schedule, HPB found that taxi drivers need to send in their taxis for servicing every month and the golden opportunity to reach out to taxi drivers is, therefore, during this time when their taxis are being serviced and the taxi drivers are waiting for the taxis to be serviced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: HPB brought health screening to the service centres and stationed health coaches there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Taxi drivers get to check in with the health coaches every month when they send their taxi for servicing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The health coaches will help the drivers understand their health screening results and customise a health action plan with specific health goals, working together with the taxi drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The programme was extended subsequently to bus captains and it was customised to address other issues that are pertinent to bus captains, such as hydration, ergonomics and stress management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As the bus captains have even more challenging work schedules, HPB and the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU) had to organise the health screening at bus depots very early in the morning with the active support of the Public Transport Operators, namely, SBS Transit and SMRT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I was there at one of these screenings, at 4.00 in the morning and I saw for myself the bus captains coming in, reporting for work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They were excited about getting screened so that they could know about their health status.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: After that, we followed up with a series of workshops and coaching at bus interchanges over a few months in order to improve their health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: More importantly, it is not only about activities, it is also about outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The outcomes, in terms of their health screening results, have improved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are very encouraged that many of our mature workers have made a real transition into a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: An SMRT bus captain who has been driving buses for the last 32 years, he took part in HPB's "Healthier Workers, Happier Workers" programme in June 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Following a first screening where he found out that he had borderline high blood pressure and a high body mass index (BMI), Mr Loh was followed up upon by his polyclinic doctor and he attended health coaching sessions at the bus interchange almost every month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: From doing little exercise, he progressed to performing about 30 sit-ups and 40 push-ups every morning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Loh and his wife have also made changes to their diet, swapping for wholemeal options and reducing their food intake.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over a period of eight months, Mr Loh has already lost 4.5 kilogrammes, which was a big step towards a healthier BMI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At the recent health screening in January 2016, Mr Loh's blood pressure returned to normal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to customise workplace health programmes for mature workers in other sectors, such as healthcare, logistics and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In particular, we want to multiply and expand the access to health education programmes by leveraging the PA's existing community and social nodes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We hope that more seniors will be encouraged to participate in preventive health and health education activities, if these are just a few steps from where they live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, bring it closer, make it more convenient and, at the same, really urging our seniors to come and participate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In several communities, we are bringing preventive health and seniors' health education right down to the Resident's Committee (RC) centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, in Bedok, a "Wellness Time" has been set aside each week in each of the four RCs in Bedok.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Seniors are invited to come to the RC regularly to take part in workshops run by community organisations on caregiving tips, mental wellness, preventive health and chronic disease management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is the seniors' personal wellness time and they also build strong friendships and provide peer support to one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, Ms Celia Teo, a retired teacher who lives in Bedok, lives alone and often found herself staying at home feeling restless.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since starting to attend the Happy Kopitiam programme as part of the Sunflower RC's Wellness Time on Fridays, Ms Teo has gained a better understanding of various health-related topics, including dementia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: She also says that she feels happier because she has something to look forward to every week at the RC, and the RC is close to her home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond physical health, cognitive activity and social interaction are also important for overall health and wellness amongst our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In Tampines Central and several other locations, we have started a weekly news sharing programme done in collaboration with journalists from the Singapore Press Holdings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These journalists from Lianhe Zaobao and Lianhe Wanbao volunteer their time to drop by the Neighbours' Hub which is a cosy corner in the void deck every Friday.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They go there to read news articles from the newspapers to our seniors and to engage our seniors in discussions over current affairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For instance, many seniors find it inconvenient to travel to SOCs to get a proper hearing test or for the fitting out of hearing aids, even though the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund subsidises such hearing aids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: An example of an integrated system of preventive health, health education and social wellness activities have also been rolled into one at Paya Lebar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: TGLC actively reaches out to the community to encourage them to drop by to check their health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is complemented by daily programming and interest groups at the Paya Lebar Wellness Centre to encourage seniors to take part in physical exercise whilst keeping in touch with neighbours and friends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is a meaningful effort that can succeed only with the support of everyone – community-based organisations, grassroots, healthcare providers, family members, employers, unions and, most of all, our seniors themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By working together in every workplace and in every neighbourhood, we can and will build a nation for ages.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is, therefore, easy for women to neglect their own health.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Diabetes is a common chronic disease and it is only becoming more common.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It adversely affects a patient's life and can lead to complications.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Being a chronic disease, the long-term medical financial burden can be high, too.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: In this regard, I would like to ask what is the Ministry's plan in promoting better women health and preventing diabetes, especially gestational diabetes, in women.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: They are usually the central figure in families, taking charge of the cooking, health appointments, caregiving activities and childbearing as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: It is thus important to ensure our women stay healthy and happy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: They are also the gender with the longer lifespan, which means they may also face the brunt of the complications of chronic illnesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: For those who are working, there will be, of course, added responsibilities to prioritise their commitments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Can I ask MOH what is the role of the Women's Health Advisory Committee and also on the following issues which, hopefully, can be reviewed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Two, tracking and monitoring our Singaporean women's health statistics which can be shared openly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: I hope that this can be a motivational element for our ladies to see the positive changes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Thirdly, more education and outreach for our ladies with diabetes since we are all on a war path against diabetes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: The prevalence is high and even higher amongst some ethnic groups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: As mentioned, our women play important roles and we do not want them to be prematurely debilitated by the complications of diabetes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: The other group to assist will be our women with gestational diabetes and a proportion of them, we know, do go on to become pre-diabetic or overt diabetic.

text: Therefore, I think a proactive approach to handle this will be necessary.

text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, you have two cuts.

text: It helps the doctor make better decisions, because they understand the patient over months and many years.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: A familiar face is often key to changing lifestyle and fighting chronic disease.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: A smoker is more likely to stop when it is a familiar face who has known him for many years asking him to quit.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: A diabetic patient is more likely to comply with medication when it is an old friend explaining why the medication is needed to save his life and to save his limbs and his organs in future.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: There is still a culture of patients going from doctor to doctor, often within the course of a single illness.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Sadly, this means no single doctor may have the full picture of the patient's condition and no single doctor may have understood the patient's illness over time.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This can lead to delays in diagnosis and treatment.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It does not help our control of chronic diseases.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our family physicians have a very important role to play and it is crucial that MOH supports family medicine and primary care, including enhancing primary care subsidies.

text: These subsidies, in addition to being enhanced, can also be structured and communicated, so that patients have peace of mind and are not afraid to be screened for chronic diseases.

text: The need and demand for Government primary care services will continue to rise, especially with the introduction of the PG Package, the CHAS programme and other subsidy schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about our Ministry's detailed plans under the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have planned a suite of initiatives along two directions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, going beyond healthcare to health by investing more in health promotion and active ageing to help seniors live longer and live well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, going beyond hospital to home and community by building up a good system of home and community-based care that can provide person-centric care for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I always tell my seniors that they need to achieve three "wellness" for successful ageing: physical wellness, mental wellness and social wellness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the Action Plan, we will step up efforts to promote seniors' health education at different levels: at the national level, in the community and at workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the national level, MOH and HPB will embark on a series of public education campaigns on seniors' health issues this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: HPB will roll out campaigns on topics, such as Seniors' Nutrition, Falls Prevention and Dementia, to raise awareness among seniors on how they can keep healthy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will launch a new National Seniors' Health Programme which is a set of "healthy ageing 101" programmes on health issues important to seniors, such as nutrition, exercise, mental wellness and chronic disease management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Seniors will be encouraged to go through this series of six basic health workshops as a start and then they can attend other additional workshops depending on their interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This set of programmes will be delivered in the community and that was elaborated earlier by Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To enable seniors to be cognitively and socially active as well, MOH has worked with MOE to establish a new National Silver Academy to enable seniors to pursue learning in diverse areas according to their interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Academy will offer new learning opportunities for seniors in three areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, Singaporeans will be able to take selected courses offered by the Institute of Technical Education (ITEs), polytechnics and universities without taking exams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The post-secondary education institutions are making selected modules from their full qualification courses available for seniors to attend without being assessed, for a token fee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Seniors will be able to sit in the same classroom and learn together with the regular students attending the course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, seniors can now receive subsidies for short courses offered by these post-secondary education institutions as well as VWOs that cover a whole range of topics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, such courses offered by the post-secondary education institutions are largely unsubsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, seniors can look forward to a wider range of courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Academy will not only include courses from educational institutions, including the two art colleges LaSalle and NAFA, but also those from community-based organisations and other ad hoc learning opportunities as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, seniors can also attend intergenerational learning programmes conducted by students in school after school hours on topics, such as technology and music.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We hope that the Academy can not only fulfil seniors' aspirations to keep learning, but also help shape a new mindset regarding ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I think having seniors learn with younger students in the same classroom will foster intergenerational interactions and also, at the same time, inspire our younger generation that learning does not stop at any age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But when our seniors grow frail eventually, we need a comprehensive range of care options to enable seniors to age in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Joan Pereira asked about ramp-up plans for eldercare services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In addition to training courses and capability building programmes, AIC is also developing a voluntary baseline assessment framework based on the Guidelines to help our providers understand how they can improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH and AIC regularly engage the sector on various fronts, such as in the development of these Guidelines and the Enhanced Nursing Home Standards, in our manpower and quality improvement councils for the sector, as well as through dialogues, such as with the Association of Private Nursing Home Operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will study ways to further strengthen our tripartite partnerships, including the suggestion by Ms K Thanaletchimi to set up an ILTC association.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms Joan Pereira also spoke about delivering home and community care in an integrated manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, this is one of our key strategies going forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, we want to train and assess a new "corps" of domestic elder carers so that they can anchor good care for seniors at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have introduced a Foreign Domestic Worker Grant and lowered the concessionary levy so that it is more affordable for caregivers of frail seniors to hire foreign domestic helpers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But some caregivers still find it difficult to obtain domestic helpers who are proficient in eldercare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The new training programme, developed in consultation with experienced nurses from nursing homes and community hospitals, includes four days of classroom learning and on-the-job training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Trainers will go to the homes to observe the domestic helpers at work and check that they can perform the required eldercare tasks competently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These pre-trained elder carers can then be deployed to families in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Existing employers who want to send their domestic helpers for this in-depth training can also contact AIC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, we will complement domestic maids with informal caregivers in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Dr Lily Neo and Ms Joan Pereira spoke about befriending and support for seniors at risk of isolation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH piloted a community befriending programme a year ago where seniors are paired with befrienders living in the neighbourhood who can visit them often, keep an eye on their condition and help them with their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since the start of the programme, some 15 communities have come on board with over 230 befriendees and almost 90 befrienders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These befrienders are given a small token to cover the costs of their befriending work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, we will further strengthen our community-based home and day care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To serve the needs of seniors more holistically, MOH has worked with some providers to pilot new Integrated Home and Day Care packages that bundle both home and centre-based care services together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, we have such a combination and that is the Singapore Programme for Integrated Care for the Elderly (SPICE) programme for frail seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are now expanding the original SPICE package to pilot three or more new care packages which offer different combinations of care services to meet the needs of seniors with a wider range of frailty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During the day, Mdm Lim attends the Peacehaven Bedok Multi-Service Centre, where she receives rehab and nursing care and does recreational activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The centre will also help her pre-pack her medications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On days when she is feeling unwell, the centre's staff will check on her at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They will also arrange for basic housekeeping services and meals delivery for her during the weekends, which are additional add-on services not included within the current SPICE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: All these services will be conveniently bundled within a single, comprehensive care package for Mdm Lim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If successful and well received by caregivers, we will scale up the packages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also test a new tool to capture seniors' needs – functional, cognitive and social – holistically, for better matching with services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fourth, we will build more and better centres to support the new care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, MOH is working with HDB to pre-build larger spaces within new Build-To-Order HDB developments to serve as "Active Ageing Hubs" or AAHs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are one-stop centres for seniors that can serve a range of needs, from active ageing programmes for ambulant and healthy seniors, to day care and rehab services for frail seniors, to "assisted living" services, such as grocery delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The size of these AAHs will depend on the space available in the developments but can be up to twice as large as the eldercare centres today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We launched the first Request-For-Proposal (RFP) for operating two AAHs at Kallang-Whampoa last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fifth, to close the last mile, we need to improve the system of transportation to care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the past year, AIC piloted a programme with ComfortDelgro to engage taxi drivers to send seniors from home to their care centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The effort is off to a promising start with 25 taxi drivers on the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More than 130 seniors have benefited from the service, and we hope to expand the service to serve 200 more seniors this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Sixth, Regional Health Systems are piloting new programmes to strengthen their support for frail patients in the post-discharge period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, SingHealth is piloting a new system of deploying its nurses to provide home nursing care to its patients living nearby, starting with Bukit Merah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have set up a National Innovation Challenge (NIC) on Active and Confident Ageing to support research and innovation in ageing-related issues, including the use of technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, MOH made two grant calls under NIC to seek innovative ideas to improve manpower productivity of home-care services and enhance dementia care in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We received close to 100 proposals and we will select the best ideas to be implemented on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ultimately, home and community care must work together with good residential care options to form a robust system of care for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Thus far, we have largely tendered out our aged care facilities individually or in pairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Going forward, we need to better integrate different forms of aged care services so that seniors can receive continuous, seamless and person-centric care even as their care needs evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There are a few objectives to this IOP scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, we want to encourage a single operator to integrate residential and non-residential aged care services into patient-centric care options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, we hope that these large tenders will enable us to grow bigger players with the economies of scale to provide better and more affordable care for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, by packaging different care services in a region into a single tender, we hope to develop strategic partners who can then partner our Regional Health Systems to provide integrated and seamless care from the acute sector to community hospital to long term care, for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: IOPs will need to demonstrate that they are able to achieve higher standards of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I assure Members that even while we roll out IOP bundles, we will continue to call smaller tenders with individual facilities and services to cater to providers who may prefer to specialise in a particular care setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our eventual aim is to develop a sizeable, diverse and resilient sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to support all players, both big and small, in developing their capabilities in this sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH and AIC have partnered SPRING Singapore to reach out to the private sector aged care providers and enable them to tap on the Capability Development Grant to embark on new manpower development or productivity initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond individual services, we need to better integrate the programmes, services and resources within each community to build a strong "community of care".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And it is for this reason that we are piloting community networks for seniors, as mentioned by Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The aim of the community network for seniors is to enable more systematic collaboration between Government agencies and community-based stakeholders, enabling them to leverage each other's strengths and resources to jointly support our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A small group of staff from different agencies will work together to drive the development of this network and there are three objectives of this community network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government agencies will coordinate our efforts with local VWOs and grassroots so that we combine forces and collectively reach out to a bigger pool of seniors, rather than visit the same seniors a few times over.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, PGAs can inform the Pioneers of relevant active ageing and social activities in the community, as part of their current house visits to explain Government schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, we want to link the programmes and services across Government agencies, VWOs and grassroots organisations together so that we can serve our seniors better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, we can join up the healthcare services provided by Regional Health Systems with the social care provided by community-based organisations to support our vulnerable seniors better in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, we want to engage stakeholders and recruit more resident volunteers in a particular community, to help their fellow elderly neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With Community Networks for Seniors, we hope to build kampungs for all ages, where our seniors can age happily, healthily and actively in place, for as long as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If we build up strong community networks over time, caregivers will also have greater peace of mind that their elderly loved ones will have many caring neighbours and agencies on the ground looking out for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about our plans to grow the healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the midst of a more uncertain economic climate, the growth in the healthcare sector will provide good job opportunities and meaningful new careers for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH is stepping up efforts to attract fresh school leavers and mid-career professionals to join the healthcare industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, we are enhancing information and outreach through career talks and exhibitions, engaging the education and career guidance (ECG) counsellors to secondary school students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also continue to support providers to recruit nurses, allied health professionals and care staff for the aged care sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH has also provided funding support to enhance the pay competitiveness of healthcare workers in VWO providers, in tandem with the pay increases in the public healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will do even more this year, to enhance recruitment for the aged care sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested recruiting retired nurses to deliver home and community care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, some of our home-care providers are already doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To better attract non-practising local nurses back to work in the growing aged care sector, we have enhanced the Return-To-Nursing scheme in April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We aim to recruit 10 mid-career talents per year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They will undergo three months of training with AIC to understand the sector before taking up senior positions like Centre Directors in the institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH will provide funding support to the institutions for the remuneration and benefits given to these mid-career talents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we explore more initiatives to grow local workforce participation in the sector, there is still a need to bring in foreign healthcare workers to augment our local supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to help these workers adapt to our practices and working environment, so that they can be effective members of our teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh spoke about home nursing providers who bring in foreign nurses under foreign domestic worker permits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The providers Assoc Prof Daniel Goh mentioned are employment agencies who bring in care aides to assist senior clients and they hold foreign domestic worker permits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In parallel with efforts to grow the workforce are efforts to deepen skills and build new capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To date, more than 7,000 ILTC staff have undergone various training, from care skills training to leadership programmes under the AIC Learning Institute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the national SkillsFuture initiative, we will introduce the Healthcare Skills Future Study Awards to support skills upgrading of the healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The awards will be opened for application from June this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH will also champion initiatives within the public healthcare sector to make our healthcare institutions age-friendly and enhance the longevity of our older experienced staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our healthcare institutions will be systematically introducing mechanisation to take away the physical strain of healthcare jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also redesign jobs, introduce FWAs and provide retraining to create more opportunities for older Singaporeans to work in the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, NUH has started a flexi-work pilot for Singaporeans to help ward nurses with basic care duties, so that the nurses can focus on clinical nursing work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Thanaletchimi and Dr Chia Shi-Lu will also be pleased to note that all healthcare clusters today have FWAs in place to help workers balance work and personal demands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These include part-time employment, compressed work week, flexible work schedules and hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, four hospitals piloted new FWAs for nurses in selected wards, where the timing of the afternoon shift was brought forward to allow the nurses to spend more time with their families and friends after work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH is currently working to facilitate electronic rostering systems, so that more FWAs for nurses can be scaled up to all public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our healthcare institutions will also strengthen workplace health programmes and introduce new retirement planning programmes for their mature workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These include pre- and post-retirement workshops, to guide older healthcare workers through career transition issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In short, despite the current economic uncertainty, the health and aged care sector is expanding and will be able to offer many different good jobs to Singaporeans of all ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked for an update on community mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, I updated the House that we will systematically strengthen our community mental health efforts in a few ways and I am pleased to report that we are making steady progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, to enhance the mental well-being of Singaporeans, HPB has rolled out initiatives to equip the public with knowledge and skills to keep mentally well and seek help early, if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, their "Working Minds" talks and workshops in workplaces impart skills on managing stress and developing resilience so that employees can perform at their best and 4,500 employees from 90 small and medium enterprises (SMEs) have participated in these workshops since they started in 2013.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Six allied health-led community teams have also been set up to support GPs by providing counselling and psycho-education to clients and caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is an increase from the 70 GP partners and nine specialist and allied health-led teams last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, we have reached out to 36 constituencies; 16 in the past one year alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Over 800 grassroots leaders, volunteers and community partners have been trained in basic mental health knowledge and symptoms of mental illness, which allows them to identify, respond and support residents with mental health challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Again, this is an increase from the 400 trained in 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: AIC has also trained over 500 staff from the ground agencies, such as HDB, Town Councils, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and Family Service Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In addition, advisors in all 89 divisions have been given a single AIC contact point for easier referral to assist residents with suspected mental health issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: AIC will be the first responder and lead in coordinating further assessment and care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To address Dr Lily Neo's suggestion, SSOs today can refer persons with suspected mental health issues to AIC for assessment, as well as help provide the necessary support if needed, as part of the overall care plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fourth, IMH is strengthening its after-care services to better support clients post-discharge, so that they could be better managed and supported to continue to live in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Together with AIC, IMH is piloting an integrated model of after-care case management for clients with moderate to complex social and healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Case managers assigned to these clients will assist in their transitional care upon discharge and link them to community support partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These after-care teams have reached out to over 150 clients since 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: IMH is also enhancing its capability to monitor higher risk patients post-discharge and ensure that they comply with follow-up treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If a patient refuses or defaults on treatment, IMH will work closely with family members, caregivers and other community partners to engage the patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nonetheless, the experience of these countries is mixed so far, and there is no robust evidence to show that community treatment orders are effective in achieving key outcomes, such as reduced hospital re-admissions, improved medication adherence and patients' quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we study such an approach, it is important that we continue to enhance access to mental health services and continuity of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We share Mr Low Thia Kiang's concern about funding for mental health, and take a calibrated approach in ensuring comparability in coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Patients requiring inpatient treatment can enjoy Government subsidies similar to other medical treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The MediShield Life claim limit and MediSave withdrawal limit for psychiatric treatments are lower, as Mr Low has said, because its bill size is generally lower as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MediFund assistance is also available for those who are unable to afford treatment, even after subsidies and MediSave and MediShield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Patients requiring outpatient mental health treatment can receive Government subsidies at our SOCs and polyclinics, which were recently enhanced for lower- to middle-income patients, who also enjoy CHAS subsidies at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Pioneers can receive special subsidies at SOCs, polyclinics and CHAS GPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: All patients can also use MediSave for psychiatric conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) and our seniors can further tap on Flexi-MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We recognise the stresses of caregiving, as highlighted by Miss Cheng Li Hui and Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, and have enhanced support for caregivers to make it easier for them to navigate our care system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Caregivers can approach AIC's AICarelinks at AIC's office and our hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are one-stop points to get information and advice on the appropriate services for their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They can also contact AIC's Singapore Silver Line for support on all matters relating to mental health and eldercare services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides the four major languages, there are dialect-speaking agents available for seniors who are more comfortable speaking in their native dialects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also put in place programmes to help patients and their caregivers transit more smoothly from the hospital to home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since 2008, AIC has care coordinators who helped patients look for services required after discharge and follow up with them to provide further support post-discharge through phone calls, home visits or both.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To ensure their well-being, we have also made respite care more accessible for caregivers and enhanced subsidies to help defray the costs of caregiving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: AIC also works closely with community touch points to look out for caregivers who may be stressed and render assistance where needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As noted by Mr Low Thia Kiang, Miss Cheng Li Hui and Dr Tan Wu Meng, the focus for our community mental health efforts going forward will be on dementia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also expanding capacity of dementia care services in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last month, I launched an effort to build a Dementia-Friendly Community in Hong Kah North, after the first such community was launched at Chong Pang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are working with other divisions, such as MacPherson, Queenstown and Bedok, to embark upon this initiative, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under this initiative, we will build up networks of Dementia Friends who are trained to recognise and provide assistance where necessary to persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also pilot a safe return system for lost seniors and step up efforts to raise public awareness, such as through AIC's dementia toolkit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We hope to encourage more communities to come together to build a dementia-friendly Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Moving on to women's health issues, I am pleased to update that I will be chairing a revamped Women's Health Committee to focus on three key health issues among women.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are increasing cancer screening uptake, promoting bone health and, of course, women cannot be left out of the war on diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: So, the third focus will be on fighting diabetes, particularly diabetes linked to obesity and gestational diabetes, which Ms Tin Pei Ling and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Promoting bone health is also important for women who are at higher risk of osteoporosis than men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Committee will also encourage women to promote good health in our families, such as by breastfeeding our infants, which may reduce the risk of obesity and, hence, diabetes for them later in life, provide them with the best possible nutrition and protect them against illnesses and allergies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A Nation for "All Ages" has to be built by all Singaporeans together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With many hands and many hearts, I am positive that we can face population ageing confidently and successfully.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is also on the rise in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We must keep our young healthy and fit, for their own sake and for the sake of a healthy Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Hence, what is the MOH's plan to address childhood obesity?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: What is the Ministry's plan also in promoting and supporting our young to stay healthy?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, they have to deal with the pressures of school.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Assessment and homework are followed by more assessment and homework.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Then, you have enrichment classes and tuition and everything culminates in examinations at the end of primary and secondary school.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They are also increasingly exposed to the digital world.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While infocommunication technology can be a great learning tool if employed correctly, this digital world also presents its own set of challenges, such as the exposure to too much unfiltered knowledge.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And the pervasiveness of social media also means that these young students sometimes find themselves the victims of cyber-bullying.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such issues used to be typically associated with teenagers, but we have to acknowledge that pre-teen students are facing these challenges as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have personally spoken to a few parents of children from this age group who are seeing psychologists to help their children deal with the stress.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, some parents feel that they should see a psychologist as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the risk of falling into mental health problems, it is usually precipitated by experiencing simultaneous multiple stressors in life.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition to those stressors mentioned above, these could also arise from problems in their family and personal relationships.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, would the Ministry consider having a decentralised community-based mental wellness facility not just for students, but for others, too?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I heard about the good team of doctors and staff in these premises and I thank them for their passion in caring for their clients.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I understand that children with mood and anxiety-related concerns, including eating disorders and relationship problems, may be referred there for therapy.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Would the Ministry also provide figures on the number of children and youths below age 18 seeking treatment at Buangkok Green?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Will the Ministry consider relocating the Buangkok Green unit to our heartlands or start new units in other locations to strengthen support for mental wellness?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: While the Government is proactively working to prevent mosquito breeding, it is not foolproof.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The risk of an infection brought in by an unsuspecting foreign carrier is always present.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We, therefore, need to look at other prevention methods.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Could the Ministry share whether there are plans to integrate dengue vaccination with other dengue control and healthcare strategies in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Could the Ministry also share whether it will invest in research into Zika, its treatment and vaccination?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu, you have two cuts, please take them together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Take the first two cuts, and take the third one, when I indicate so.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: While we are understandably concerned about the impact of chronic diseases on the population, such as diabetes, which we have been hearing about, we must remain vigilant to the continued threat of infectious diseases, in particular, new and emerging ones.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Our experience with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) at the turn of the millennium has shown us the devastating impact of a previously unrecognised infectious disease and the immense human, social and economic cost.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: More than a decade later, the world continues to be besieged by the threat of emerging infectious pathogens: bird flu, swine flu, Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS), Ebola and, more recently, the Zika virus.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: MERS remains a threat in the Middle East and had a devastating though fortunately limited outbreak in South Korea last year.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I commend the Ministry on how it has increased our preparedness to deal with such threats since the SARS epidemic, and Singapore has thus far been spared similar crises, through a combination of vigilance, border controls and perhaps through a measure of good fortune.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Results of quality-of-care reviews, patient satisfaction surveys, average costs of hospitalisation for common procedures are readily available, and patients can now access their personal health information online.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Can this added transparency be harnessed to improve healthcare delivery, in terms of efficiency, quality and also cost containment?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Many are concerned about the cost of private healthcare and also of IP premiums, notwithstanding the recently announced Standard B1 plans that aim to provide a reasonable benchmark for IPs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOH remains committed to reinforcing the core pillars of a quality healthcare system for our population.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This encompasses taking a closer look at the fundamentals of our healthcare system, including developing better preventive health services for our young and strengthening primary care.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There is a rising prevalence of chronic diseases amongst our population.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are concerned about this increasing prevalence, as these conditions can lead to serious complications if not well-managed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, complications faced by poorly-controlled diabetic patients include kidney failure, stroke, heart attack, blindness and even lower limb amputations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The risk of chronic diseases in general can be lowered through simple lifestyle changes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Choosing to live healthily is a habit that we should inculcate from a young age.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As pointed out by Ms Tin Pei Ling, it is vital that we go upstream and enhance preventive health services that encourage the formation of healthy habits in our children and youths, even as we continue to step up our efforts in promoting health screening among older adults.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: All of us have a role to play in keeping our young healthy and fit, especially parents and caregivers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They role-model healthy living, nurture a healthy home environment, influence and guide children to form healthy habits, which, hopefully, will continue through adulthood.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In Singapore, we have had a comprehensive school health service since 1921, which underpins the good public health achieved today.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The HPB's current strategies and close collaboration with the schools in encouraging students to adopt a healthy lifestyle have served us well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, trained professional nurses are stationed full-time in selected secondary schools and post-secondary institutions under the Student Health Advisor (SHA) programme, to provide advice on weight management and smoking cessation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: One successful story is that of Ms Tan Su Kheng.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For many years, Su Kheng put up with jokes and comments about her weight, which affected her self-esteem.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Last year, she joined her school's weight management intervention programme, which helped to kick-start her journey towards a healthier life.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On top of receiving many practical tips on healthy living, Su Kheng found additional support through her SHA, who taught her how to incorporate exercise into her busy student life.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Apart from exercising thrice a week, she walks home and takes the stairs every day, instead of taking the bus and using the lift respectively.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The journey to staying healthy can be challenging.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, I am inspired by what Su Kheng relates to us about her experience.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And I quote, "Whenever I feel like giving up, I will tell myself that although I may not be there yet, I am one step closer to success than yesterday." I am happy to share that with her perseverance and encouragement from her SHA, Su Kheng has lost over 20 kilogrammes in just one year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I hear that family and friends have even started approaching her for tips on healthy living.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Studies have shown that childhood obesity is likely to persist and progress into adulthood.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This results in individuals being at higher risks of developing chronic diseases, such as diabetes and hypertension.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: An overseas study revealed that those with childhood obesity are four times more likely to be at risk of developing hypertension in adulthood when compared to their non-obese peers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is, therefore, critical that we curb the rising rates of childhood obesity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: A local survey showed that most students are engaging in less physical activities and becoming more sedentary.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Based on past surveys, only about 10% of mainstream or ITE students and 20% of polytechnic students had sufficient physical activity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, the prevalence of myopia in our children is one of the highest in the world.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is undesirable as poor eyesight from myopia can impact learning.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Poor oral health affects the nutrition, growth and development of our children.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are concerned and are keen to tackle the pervasion of these trends among our young.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Apart from their physical growth and development, we will also further strengthen our efforts to help our young to build up their mental resilience to better cope with the stressors of life.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Darryl David raised concerns on the mental resilience and well-being of our youths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To comprehensively address the multifaceted aspects of student mental health concerns, we have adopted a three-pronged approach, comprising knowledge and skills-building, facilitating access and referral to mental health services, and parental engagement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOE and HPB have introduced programmes to provide educators with basic knowledge on common issues faced by our youths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Educators are also equipped with the ability to detect early warning signs and skills to provide appropriate support and referrals to services and resources in the school setting.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These programmes have also groomed youth opinion leaders on health, by arming them with knowledge on health and well-being, mental health concerns and youth advocacy.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Darryl David also suggested having community-based mental wellness facilities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As Senior Minister of State Amy Khor mentioned earlier, we are steadily building up our mental health services and support networks within the community to identify and help persons with mental health concerns.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is important for us to work upstream to lay strong foundations for our young to lead healthier and more productive lives, starting from those as young as two years old.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The NurtureSG Taskforce will focus on three main areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, we will look into developing new strategies and strengthening existing programmes to address salient health issues and negative trends among children and youths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Next, we want to reinforce health promotion efforts at the tertiary institutions so that young Singaporeans will maintain healthy habits beyond the school-going age and well after entering the workforce.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In particular, we will engage students, educators, parents, caregivers and even the private sector, such as food establishments, to create a healthier environment for our children.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To Miss Cheng Li Hui's comments, children are referred to the hospitals for both developmental and mental health conditions by polyclinics, GPs, paediatricians, primary schools and REACH, which stands for Response, Early Assessment and intervention in Community mental Health teams.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Besides the Child Guidance clinics at Buangkok View and Outram Road, mental health services for children and youths are also available in other hospitals, such as NUH, Singapore General Hospital (SGH) and KK Hospital.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These services typically include assessment, diagnosis and multidisciplinary management of patients up to the age of 18, but may continue to follow up with them beyond this, where appropriate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The subsidies for these services are in line with existing SOC subsidies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Empowering and teaching our young to lead healthier lives are only one part of the equation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As our population ages and healthcare needs continue to rise, we must reshape the way we approach healthcare.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Primary care is the foundation of any healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We aim to strengthen its place in our healthcare system, to be the first and continuous line of care.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about the role of the family doctor.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Overseas studies have shown that care continuity by a regular family doctor results in better care outcomes for patients.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These include decreased hospitalisations and emergency department visits.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
